title: OSHA general industry personal protective equipment practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry PPE practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart I. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Under 1910.132(d), who must assess the workplace to determine whether hazards are present, or likely to be present, that make PPE necessary?

options.A: The employer
options.B: Each employee, for their own work area
options.C: An OSHA compliance officer
options.D: The PPE manufacturer

questions.explanation: "The employer shall assess the workplace to determine if hazards are present, or are likely to be present, which necessitate the use of personal protective equipment (PPE)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall assess the workplace to determine if hazards are present, or are likely to be present, which necessitate the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

questions.question: How must the employer verify that the required workplace hazard assessment has been performed?

options.A: By telephoning the nearest OSHA area office
options.B: By posting the PPE list at the entrance
options.C: Through a written certification
options.D: By having each employee initial the PPE they receive

questions.explanation: The employer must verify the assessment "through a written certification that identifies the workplace evaluated; the person certifying that the evaluation has been performed; the date(s) of the hazard assessment; and, which identifies the document as a certification of hazard assessment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall verify that the required workplace hazard assessment has been performed through a written certification that identifies the workplace evaluated; the person certifying that the evaluation has been performed; the date(s) of the hazard assessment; and, which identifies the document as a certification of hazard assessment.

questions.question: What does 1910.132 say about defective or damaged personal protective equipment?

options.A: It may be used until the end of the shift
options.B: It may be used if a supervisor approves
options.C: It may be used for tasks with low hazards
options.D: It shall not be used

questions.explanation: 1910.132(e) is direct: "Defective or damaged personal protective equipment shall not be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Defective or damaged personal protective equipment shall not be used.

questions.question: Before an employee is allowed to perform work requiring PPE, what must the employee demonstrate?

options.A: That they bought PPE approved by OSHA
options.B: An understanding of the training and the ability to use PPE properly
options.C: That they have worked in the trade for one year
options.D: That they passed a written exam given by OSHA

questions.explanation: Each affected employee "shall demonstrate an understanding of the training specified in paragraph (f)(1) of this section, and the ability to use PPE properly, before being allowed to perform work requiring the use of PPE."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each affected employee shall demonstrate an understanding of the training specified in paragraph (f)(1) of this section, and the ability to use PPE properly, before being allowed to perform work requiring the use of PPE.

questions.question: Under 1910.132(g), the hazard assessment and training paragraphs of 1910.132 (paragraphs (d) and (f)) apply only to certain sections. Which section is one of them?

options.A: 1910.134, Respiratory protection
options.B: 1910.137, Electrical protective equipment
options.C: 1910.136, Foot protection
options.D: 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Paragraphs (d) and (f) of this section apply only to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140. Paragraphs (d) and (f) of this section do not apply to §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137.

questions.question: When is an employer not required to pay for replacement PPE?

options.A: When the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE
options.B: When the PPE wore out through normal use
options.C: When the PPE was replaced within the first year
options.D: When the employee works fewer than 40 hours a week

questions.explanation: "The employer must pay for replacement PPE, except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer must pay for replacement PPE, except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE.

questions.question: Under 1910.132(h), which of these is the employer not required to pay for?

options.A: Protective helmets required by 1910.135
options.B: Respirators required by 1910.134
options.C: Replacement PPE after normal wear
options.D: Sunscreen used solely for protection from weather

questions.explanation: The employer is not required to pay for "Ordinary clothing, skin creams, or other items, used solely for protection from weather," which the rule says includes "ordinary sunglasses, and sunscreen."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Ordinary clothing, skin creams, or other items, used solely for protection from weather, such as winter coats, jackets, gloves, parkas, rubber boots, hats, raincoats, ordinary sunglasses, and sunscreen.

questions.question: When may an employer require an employee to provide or pay for their own PPE?

options.A: Whenever the employee agrees in writing
options.B: Only when the PPE is excepted by paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(5)
options.C: Whenever the employee is in a probationary period
options.D: Whenever the PPE will also be used at home

questions.explanation: "The employer shall not require an employee to provide or pay for his or her own PPE, unless the PPE is excepted by paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(5) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall not require an employee to provide or pay for his or her own PPE, unless the PPE is excepted by paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(5) of this section.

questions.question: When must an employee's eye protection provide side protection?

options.A: Only when the employee wears prescription lenses
options.B: When there is a hazard from flying objects
options.C: Only during welding
options.D: Only when working outdoors

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure each affected employee "uses eye protection that provides side protection when there is a hazard from flying objects."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.133, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: uses eye protection that provides side protection when there is a hazard from flying objects.

questions.question: An employee who wears prescription lenses works in an operation that involves eye hazards. What must the employee wear?

options.A: Their everyday prescription glasses, with nothing added
options.B: Tinted prescription lenses instead of eye protection
options.C: Contact lenses in place of eye protection
options.D: Eye protection that incorporates the prescription, or that fits over the prescription lenses without disturbing either

questions.explanation: The employee "wears eye protection that incorporates the prescription in its design, or wears eye protection that can be worn over the prescription lenses without disturbing the proper position of the prescription lenses or the protective lenses."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.133, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: wears eye protection that incorporates the prescription in its design, or wears eye protection that can be worn over the prescription lenses without disturbing the proper position of the prescription lenses or the protective lenses.

questions.question: Under 1910.135, when must an affected employee wear a protective helmet?

options.A: When working in areas where there is a potential for injury to the head from falling objects
options.B: Only when working more than 10 feet above the ground
options.C: Only when the employee requests one
options.D: Only in areas with posted noise warnings

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure each affected employee "wears a protective helmet when working in areas where there is a potential for injury to the head from falling objects."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.135, Head protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall ensure that each affected employee wears a protective helmet when working in areas where there is a potential for injury to the head from falling objects.

questions.question: Which situation calls for protective footwear under 1910.136?

options.A: Any shift longer than 8 hours
options.B: Work done only on carpeted floors
options.C: A danger of foot injuries due to falling or rolling objects
options.D: Any job that requires standing

questions.explanation: Protective footwear is required "when working in areas where there is a danger of foot injuries due to falling or rolling objects, or objects piercing the sole," or when it will protect against a remaining electrical hazard.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.136, Foot protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: uses protective footwear when working in areas where there is a danger of foot injuries due to falling or rolling objects, or objects piercing the sole

questions.question: On what must employers base their selection of hand protection?

options.A: An evaluation of the hand protection's performance characteristics relative to the tasks, conditions, duration of use and hazards
options.B: The lowest available price
options.C: The glove color the employee prefers
options.D: Whatever brand was used at the employee's last job

questions.explanation: "Employers shall base the selection of the appropriate hand protection on an evaluation of the performance characteristics of the hand protection relative to the task(s) to be performed, conditions present, duration of use, and the hazards and potential hazards identified."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.138, Hand protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employers shall base the selection of the appropriate hand protection on an evaluation of the performance characteristics of the hand protection relative to the task(s) to be performed, conditions present, duration of use, and the hazards and potential hazards identified.

questions.question: In controlling diseases caused by breathing contaminated air, what does 1910.134 name as the primary objective?

options.A: Giving every employee a dust mask
options.B: Limiting shifts to 4 hours
options.C: Testing employees' lungs every month
options.D: Preventing atmospheric contamination, as far as feasible by accepted engineering control measures

questions.explanation: "The primary objective shall be to prevent atmospheric contamination," accomplished "as far as feasible by accepted engineering control measures." "When effective engineering controls are not feasible, or while they are being instituted, appropriate respirators shall be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the primary objective shall be to prevent atmospheric contamination. This shall be accomplished as far as feasible by accepted engineering control measures (for example, enclosure or confinement of the operation, general and local ventilation, and substitution of less toxic materials). When effective engineering controls are not feasible, or while they are being instituted, appropriate respirators shall be used pursuant to this section.

questions.question: An employee's only respirator use is the voluntary use of filtering facepieces (dust masks). What does 1910.134 say about including that employee in the written respiratory protection program?

options.A: The employee must be included and fit tested annually
options.B: The employee must be included after 30 days of use
options.C: Employers are not required to include that employee in the written program
options.D: The employee must be included only if they work night shifts

questions.explanation: "Employers are not required to include in a written respiratory protection program those employees whose only use of respirators involves the voluntary use of filtering facepieces (dust masks)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employers are not required to include in a written respiratory protection program those employees whose only use of respirators involves the voluntary use of filtering facepieces (dust masks).

questions.question: If an employer determines that voluntary respirator use is permissible, what must the employer give the respirator users?

options.A: A copy of the employer's insurance policy
options.B: The information contained in appendix D to 1910.134
options.C: A NIOSH certification card
options.D: A list of OSHA inspectors in the area

questions.explanation: "If the employer determines that any voluntary respirator use is permissible, the employer shall provide the respirator users with the information contained in appendix D to this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the employer determines that any voluntary respirator use is permissible, the employer shall provide the respirator users with the information contained in appendix D to this section

questions.question: When must the employer provide the medical evaluation of an employee's ability to use a respirator?

options.A: Before the employee is fit tested or required to use the respirator in the workplace
options.B: Within 90 days after the employee starts using the respirator
options.C: Only after the employee reports symptoms
options.D: Only once the employee has used the respirator for a year

questions.explanation: The employer must provide the medical evaluation "before the employee is fit tested or required to use the respirator in the workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall provide a medical evaluation to determine the employee's ability to use a respirator, before the employee is fit tested or required to use the respirator in the workplace.

questions.question: After the initial fit test, how often at minimum must an employee using a tight-fitting facepiece respirator be fit tested again, if nothing else changes?

options.A: Every 3 years
options.B: Every 2 years
options.C: Only once, at hire
options.D: At least annually

questions.explanation: The employee must be fit tested "prior to initial use of the respirator, whenever a different respirator facepiece (size, style, model or make) is used, and at least annually thereafter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: is fit tested prior to initial use of the respirator, whenever a different respirator facepiece (size, style, model or make) is used, and at least annually thereafter.

questions.question: Under 1910.134(g), an employee has facial hair that comes between the sealing surface of the facepiece and the face. What does the rule say about tight-fitting facepiece respirators for this employee?

options.A: They may be worn if the employee does a user seal check
options.B: They may be worn for up to 2 hours a day
options.C: The employer shall not permit them to be worn by this employee
options.D: They may be worn if a supervisor signs off

questions.explanation: "The employer shall not permit respirators with tight-fitting facepieces to be worn by employees who have" facial hair "that comes between the sealing surface of the facepiece and the face or that interferes with valve function."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall not permit respirators with tight-fitting facepieces to be worn by employees who have: (A) Facial hair that comes between the sealing surface of the facepiece and the face or that interferes with valve function

questions.question: How often must employees perform a user seal check on a tight-fitting respirator?

options.A: Once a month
options.B: Each time they put on the respirator
options.C: Only during the annual fit test
options.D: Only when the respirator is new

questions.explanation: For all tight-fitting respirators, the employer must ensure "that employees perform a user seal check each time they put on the respirator," using the procedures in appendix B-1 or manufacturer-recommended procedures that the employer demonstrates are as effective.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For all tight-fitting respirators, the employer shall ensure that employees perform a user seal check each time they put on the respirator using the procedures in appendix B-1 or procedures recommended by the respirator manufacturer that the employer demonstrates are as effective as those in appendix B-1 of this section.
